intro.title: Orders List Page
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an orders list page that displays a collection of orders in a clean, organized table. You'll learn how to use Angular components to structure your page and TypeScript to define the data model for your orders. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript interfaces, and Angular's template syntax for displaying data. By the end, you'll have a functional page that shows order details like ID, customer name, and status in a structured format.
intro.usecase: The orders list page pattern is fundamental to e-commerce platforms, admin dashboards, and business management systems. You'll see this in Shopify's order management interface, Amazon Seller Central's order tracking, and restaurant POS systems displaying pending orders. As a developer, you'll implement similar pages for customer support portals to view ticket queues, inventory systems to track shipments, and financial platforms to monitor transactions. This pattern combines data fetching, state management, and user interaction in a practical, reusable component structure.
